question: WHO and IYCF guidelines recommend introducing complementary foods at exactly 6 months of age, while continuing breastfeeding up to 2 years or beyond.

l10n.wrongAnswerMessage: This is true. WHO/IYCF guidelines specify 6 months as the recommended age to start complementary foods, with continued breastfeeding to 2 years. Introducing foods too early (before 4 months) increases infection risk; delaying beyond 7 months risks growth faltering.
l10n.correctAnswerMessage: Correct. WHO recommends introducing complementary foods at 6 months (not before 4 months, not delayed beyond 6–7 months) alongside continued breastfeeding until at least 2 years. The 6-month threshold is when breast milk alone no longer meets energy and micronutrient needs.
